examples.ko: 젖은 수건은 건조대에 널어야 빨리 말라요.
examples.en: Wet towels dry faster if you hang them on a drying rack.
I put a laundry drying rack on the balcony.
The rack folds, so it takes up less space.
I'm planning to buy a folding drying rack.
I hung the socks neatly on the drying rack.

examples.ko: 건조대에 빨래가 너무 많아서 잘 안 말라요.
examples.en: There's too much laundry on the rack, so it isn't drying well.

explain: 빨래나 그릇을 널어 말리는 틀이에요. '빨래 건조대', '식기 건조대'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 구별해요. 기계로 말리는 '건조기'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I hung the clothes on the drying rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 말리는 건조대라고 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear it's the rack for drying laundry.

phrases.example: 씻은 그릇은 식기 건조대에 올려 놓아요.
phrases.en: I put washed dishes on the dish rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주방에서 그릇을 말리는 틀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the kitchen rack for drying dishes.

phrases.en: I set up the drying rack before doing the laundry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 접이식 건조대를 쓸 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when using a folding drying rack.

explain_en: It is a frame for hanging laundry or dishes to dry. Words are added in front to specify, as in '빨래 건조대' and '식기 건조대'. It is different from a '건조기', the machine dryer.

examples.en: Please leave your valuables in the hotel safe.
I left my valuables behind when I got off, so I went back.
I put my bag in the valuables locker.

examples.ko: 귀중품이 든 가방은 항상 몸에 지니세요.
examples.en: Always keep the bag with your valuables on you.
There weren't even any valuables at home, but a thief broke in.
The more expensive the valuables, the more carefully you should store them.

explain: 현금, 보석, 중요한 서류처럼 잃어버리면 곤란한 물건을 묶어서 불러요. 호텔, 비행기, 사우나 같은 곳의 안내문에서 '귀중품은 직접 보관해 주세요'라는 말을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I left my valuables at the hotel front desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전한 곳에 보관해 달라고 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you hand valuables over for safekeeping.

phrases.en: Please take your valuables with you before you get off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잃어버리지 않게 가지고 다닐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make sure to keep your valuables with you.

phrases.example: 방 안의 귀중품 보관함에 여권을 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I put my passport in the valuables safe in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔이나 사우나에서 보는 안내 표지에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on signs at hotels and saunas.

explain_en: It groups items that would be a problem to lose, such as cash, jewelry and important documents. You often see notices like '귀중품은 직접 보관해 주세요' at hotels, on planes and in saunas.

examples.ko: 벽에 나사못을 네 개 박아서 선반을 달았어요.
examples.en: I put four screws into the wall and hung a shelf.
The screws are loose, so the chair keeps wobbling.

examples.ko: 나사못 길이가 너무 짧아서 다시 사러 가야 해요.
examples.en: The screws are too short, so I have to go buy them again.
Turn the screw with a screwdriver and tighten it firmly.
There is a screw on the floor, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 책상은 나사못 없이도 조립할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can assemble this desk even without screws.

explain: '못'은 망치로 박고 나사못은 드라이버로 돌려서 박아요. 일상에서는 줄여서 '나사'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I drove a screw into the wall with a screwdriver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나사못을 고정할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for fixing a screw in place.

phrases.en: I tightened the screws on the chair leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헐거워진 나사를 꽉 돌릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for tightening a loose screw.

phrases.en: I loosened the screws on the cover and opened it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조이는 것의 반대로, 돌려서 빼거나 헐겁게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of tightening: loosening or removing a screw.

explain_en: A '못' (nail) is hammered in, while a 나사못 is turned in with a screwdriver. In daily talk people often shorten it to just '나사'.

examples.en: I screwed the nut onto the bolt.
The chair wobbles because the nut has come loose.
I tightened the nut firmly with a wrench.
One of the bicycle wheel nuts is missing.
Nuts and bolts are always used as a pair.

examples.ko: 이 부품은 크기가 달라서 맞는 너트를 따로 사야 해요.
examples.en: This part is a different size, so you need to buy a matching nut separately.

explain: '너트'는 영어 nut에서 왔지만 한국어에서는 볼트에 끼우는 쇠 부품만 가리켜요. 먹는 견과류는 '견과'나 '땅콩', '호두'처럼 따로 불러요. '너트를 조이다', '너트를 풀다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I tightened the nut on the chair leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헐거운 부품을 단단하게 돌려 고정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when turning a loose part until it is firmly fixed.

phrases.en: I loosened the nuts on the wheel and changed the tire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조여 있던 너트를 돌려서 빼거나 헐겁게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for turning a tightened nut to loosen or remove it.

phrases.en: I bought a bolt and nut at the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 부품은 짝이라서 보통 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: These two parts work as a pair, so they are usually mentioned together.

explain_en: 너트 comes from English nut, but in Korean it refers only to the metal part that screws onto a bolt. Nuts you eat are called 견과 or by their own names like 땅콩 and 호두. People say 너트를 조이다 and 너트를 풀다.

examples.en: When cleaning, I wipe the floor with a mop.
The mop got dirty, so I washed it in water.

examples.ko: 교실 청소 당번이 대걸레를 들고 왔어요.
examples.en: The student on cleaning duty came in carrying a mop.

examples.ko: 이 대걸레는 손잡이가 길어서 허리를 안 굽혀도 돼요.
examples.en: This mop has a long handle, so you don't have to bend your back.

examples.ko: 대걸레 물이 너무 더러워서 새로 갈았어요.
examples.en: The mop water was too dirty, so I changed it.
I bought a mop at the mart.

explain: 긴 막대가 달려서 서서 바닥을 닦는 걸레예요. 손으로 쥐고 닦는 '걸레'와 구분해서 말해요. '밀대'나 '밀대 걸레'라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: It's easy to clean the floor with a mop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대걸레'와 같은 물건을 가리키는 다른 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is another word for the same thing.

phrases.en: I mop the living room every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '-로'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used with the tool particle '-ro'.

phrases.en: After cleaning, I washed the mop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소 후 도구를 씻을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is common when washing the tool after cleaning.

explain_en: It is a cleaning cloth on a long handle that lets you wipe the floor while standing. People distinguish it from a hand-held '걸레'. It is also called '밀대' or '밀대 걸레'.

examples.en: I put the screwdriver in the tool box.
I opened the tool box, and there was no hammer.

examples.ko: 도구함이 너무 무거워서 혼자 못 들겠어요.
examples.en: The tool box is so heavy that I can't lift it alone.
I should tidy up the tool box.
There is a small tool box in the car trunk.

examples.ko: 이 도구함에는 기본 공구가 다 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This tool box has all the basic tools in it.

explain: 공구나 도구를 넣어 두는 상자예요. 비슷한 말로 '공구함'이 있고, 옛날식으로 '연장통'이라고도 해요. 집에서는 못, 망치, 드라이버 같은 것을 넣어 두는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: I took a screwdriver out of the toolbox.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도구함'과 비슷한 말로, 공구를 넣는 상자에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word to '도구함', for a box holding tools.

phrases.en: Grandfather keeps a hammer in his toolbox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날식 말이라 어른들이 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An old-fashioned word used more by older people.

phrases.en: Please put it in the toolbox after you use it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 정리할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when tidying things.

explain_en: It is a box for keeping tools. Similar words are '공구함' and, in an older style, '연장통'. At home it holds things like nails, a hammer and a screwdriver.

examples.en: I wallpapered the room myself over the weekend.

examples.ko: 벽을 도배하려면 먼저 낡은 벽지를 떼야 해요.
examples.en: To wallpaper a wall, you first have to peel off the old wallpaper.

examples.ko: 도배한 지 얼마 안 돼서 방이 깨끗해요.
examples.en: It has not been long since the wallpapering, so the room is clean.
My father wallpapered the living room by himself.

examples.ko: 이사 오기 전에 집을 도배해 놓았어요.
examples.en: I had the house wallpapered before moving in.

examples.ko: 내일 집을 도배할 사람이 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: The person who will wallpaper the house is coming tomorrow.

explain: 벽은 '도배하다', 바닥은 '장판을 깔다'라고 말해요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '벽지', '풀'이에요. 인터넷에서는 글이나 댓글을 계속 올려 화면을 가득 채우는 것도 '도배하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 누가 같은 광고 글로 게시판을 도배했어요.
phrases.en: flood a bulletin board with the same posts
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 같은 글이나 댓글을 계속 올려 화면을 가득 채운다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Filling a page online by posting the same message or comments repeatedly.

explain_en: Walls are '도배하다' and floors are '장판을 깔다'. Related words are '벽지' and '풀'. Online, filling a page by posting the same posts or comments over and over is also '도배하다'.

examples.en: I installed an air conditioner at home.
I install a new app on my phone.

examples.ko: 내일 기사님이 와서 인터넷을 설치할 거예요.
examples.en: Tomorrow a technician will come and set up the internet.
It takes about thirty minutes to install.
After installing the program, I turned off the computer.
A fire extinguisher must be installed in this building.

explain: 앱과 프로그램, 에어컨, 카메라 같은 기계를 자리에 놓고 쓸 수 있게 할 때 써요. 앱은 '설치하다'로 받고, 지울 때는 '삭제하다'를 써요. 짝말은 '설치되다'예요.

phrases.en: Please install the air conditioner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 설치를 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone else to install something.

phrases.en: I installed a program on my computer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 휴대폰에 프로그램을 넣을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for putting software on a computer or phone.

phrases.en: An elevator is installed in the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 설치된 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something that is already installed.

explain_en: Used for apps and programs as well as machines like air conditioners and cameras, when you put them in place so they can be used. For apps, the opposite is '삭제하다' (delete). The passive partner is '설치되다'.

en: to wash off; to rinse; to cleanse

examples.en: I wash vegetables under running water.
Yesterday I took out the filter and washed it clean.

examples.ko: 일주일에 한 번 세탁기를 세척할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll clean the washing machine once a week.

examples.ko: 세척한 컵은 거꾸로 두면 빨리 말라요.
examples.en: Cups you have washed dry faster if you turn them upside down.

examples.ko: 상처를 세척하지 않으면 염증이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't clean a wound, it can get infected.
Please clean your glasses with a soft cloth.

explain: '세척하다'는 '씻다'보다 딱딱하고, 기계·도구·과일처럼 깨끗이 해야 하는 대상에 어울려요. 사람의 손이나 얼굴에는 거의 안 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '씻다'가 먼저 나와요.

phrases.en: I wash fruit well before eating it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest and most common everyday word.

phrases.en: Please wash the used cup with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 설명서에서 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request often seen in notices and manuals.

phrases.en: After washing the filter, put it back in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씻은 다음에 할 일을 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link what you do after washing.

explain_en: 세척하다 is stiffer than 씻다 and fits things that need to be made clean, like machines, tools, and fruit. It is rarely used for a person's hands or face. In daily conversation 씻다 comes up first.

examples.en: I cut my nails short with nail clippers.
Could you lend me your nail clippers?
There is a small pair of nail clippers in my bag.
The new nail clippers cut really well.
I packed nail clippers when I went on the trip.
I needed to buy nail clippers too, but I forgot.

explain: '깎다'에서 나온 말이라 '손톱깎이'로 써요. '손톱깍이'는 틀린 철자예요. '손톱을 깎다'와 함께 알아 두면 쉬워요.

phrases.example: 여행 가방에 넣을 작은 손톱깎이를 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a small nail clipper to put in my travel bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 앞에 붙여 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put a size word in front.

phrases.en: The nail clippers are in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 어디 있는지 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the item is.
phrases.en_equiv: nail clippers are in the drawer

phrases.en: I carefully trimmed the baby's nails with baby nail clippers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-용'을 붙이면 누가 쓰는 물건인지 알려 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-용' tells who the item is for.

explain_en: It comes from the verb '깎다', so the correct spelling is 손톱깎이; '손톱깍이' is a misspelling. It is easy to remember together with '손톱을 깎다' (to cut one's nails).

examples.en: I was so tired that I fell asleep as soon as I lay down on the bedding.

examples.ko: 손님이 오기 전에 이부자리를 깔아 놓았어요.
examples.en: I laid out the bedding before the guest arrived.
When I get up in the morning, I fold up my bedding right away.
The bedding was damp, so I hung it out in the sun.

examples.ko: 여행 가방에 이부자리까지 넣을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't fit bedding into my travel bag too.
The bedding spread on the warmest part of the floor is really warm.

explain: '이불'은 덮는 것만 가리키지만 '이부자리'는 요와 이불, 보통 베개까지 잠자리 한 벌을 말해요. '깔다', '펴다', '개다'와 함께 자주 써요. 침대보다는 바닥에 까는 잠자리가 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I lay out my bedding on the floor before going to sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠자리를 준비할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting the bed ready for sleep.

phrases.en: I got up in the morning and folded up my bedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자고 일어난 뒤 잠자리를 접어서 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when folding up bedding after getting up.

phrases.en: After the guest left, I tidied up the bedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개다'보다 넓게 잠자리를 치우는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 개다, covering tidying up the bed in general.

explain_en: '이불' is only the cover you put over yourself, while '이부자리' means the whole set: mattress pad, quilt and usually the pillow. It is often used with '깔다', '펴다' and '개다'. It fits floor bedding better than a bed.

examples.en: The lock is rusty and the key won't go in.
I put a small lock on the drawer.
Lock your bike to the pole with a lock.
I forgot the lock's combination.

examples.ko: 가방 지퍼에 채운 자물쇠는 열쇠로 열어요.
examples.en: I open the lock on my bag's zipper with a key.

examples.ko: 대문에 자물쇠가 잠겨 있어서 들어갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The gate was padlocked, so I couldn't get in.

explain: 자물쇠는 잠그는 쪽, 열쇠는 여는 쪽이라서 '자물쇠와 열쇠'로 짝을 이뤄 말해요. '자물쇠를 채우다', '자물쇠를 열다'처럼 써요. 문을 여닫을 때 잡는 부분은 '문고리'나 '손잡이'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이건 비밀이니까 입에 자물쇠를 채워 주세요.
phrases.en: keep your mouth shut
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않고 비밀을 지킨다는 뜻이에요. 부탁하거나 다짐할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to say nothing and keep a secret. People use it when asking someone to stay quiet or when promising to.

explain_en: A 자물쇠 is the part that locks, and a 열쇠 is the key that opens it, so the two are often said together as '자물쇠와 열쇠'. Common phrases are '자물쇠를 채우다' (put on a lock) and '자물쇠를 열다' (open a lock). The part you grab to open and close a door is the '문고리' or '손잡이'.

examples.en: I laid new flooring on the room floor.
The flooring is torn, so I need to replace it.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 따뜻한 장판 위에서 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: In winter it's nice to sleep on warm floor covering.

examples.ko: 장판에 뜨거운 냄비를 올리면 자국이 남아요.
examples.en: If you put a hot pot on the flooring, it leaves a mark.
Before moving, I picked the flooring color.
An old newspaper turned up from under the flooring.

explain: 한국식 온돌방 바닥에 까는 종이나 비닐 같은 바닥재예요. 나무로 된 바닥은 '마루'이고, '카펫'은 푹신한 천이에요. 요즘 새 집에서는 '바닥재'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I chose a wood-pattern floor covering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장판'보다 넓은 말로, 장판·마루·타일처럼 바닥에 까는 재료를 두루 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 장판; it covers any material laid on a floor, such as vinyl flooring, wood, or tile.

phrases.en: I changed the flooring before moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 바닥을 새것으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when replacing old flooring with new.

phrases.example: 겨울에는 따뜻한 장판 위에 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: In winter I sit on the warm floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥에 앉거나 눕는 장면에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when sitting or lying on the floor.

explain_en: It is the paper or vinyl floor covering laid on a Korean ondol room floor. Wooden floors are 마루, and a 카펫 is a soft carpet. In newer homes people also say 바닥재.

dis.h: vinyl sheet laid over a room floor

p.n: 바닥 is the general floor; 장판 is the covering on it.

examples.en: The paper folds neatly in half.

examples.ko: 우산이 접히지 않아서 가방에 못 넣었어요.
examples.en: The umbrella wouldn't fold, so I couldn't put it in my bag.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 접혀서 차에 쉽게 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This chair folds up, so it's easy to load into a car.
I bought a desk whose legs fold.
The wind made the umbrella suddenly fold shut.

examples.ko: 이 지도는 아주 작게 접힐 거예요.
examples.en: This map will fold up very small.

explain: '접다'는 내가 접는 것이고 '접히다'는 저절로, 또는 힘을 받아서 접어지는 거예요. 그래서 '종이를 접다'가 '종이가 접히다'가 되면서 조사가 '를'에서 '가'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: The corner of the book is folded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 접힌 상태가 계속될 때 '-아/어 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아/어 있다' to show the folded state continues.

phrases.en: This chair doesn't fold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 접을 수 없는 물건을 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form for things that can't be folded.

phrases.en: This phone folds in half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 접히는지 말할 때 '반으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '반으로' to say how something folds.

explain_en: 접다 is when someone folds something; 접히다 is when it gets folded by itself or by force. So the particle changes from 를 to 가: '종이를 접다' becomes '종이가 접히다'.

examples.en: I put the flowerpot on the windowsill.
The cat sits on the windowsill and looks outside.
A lot of dust has piled up on the windowsill.
It rained, so the windowsill is all wet.

examples.ko: 창턱에 놓인 화분에는 고운 모래가 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Fine sand is spread in the pot on the windowsill.
The windowsill is narrow, so I can't put things on it.

explain: 창문 아래쪽에 가로로 튀어나온 턱이에요. 창문 둘레의 틀은 '창틀', 창문 근처 자리는 '창가'라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.example: 창턱 위에 책이 몇 권 있어요.
phrases.en: There are a few books on the windowsill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창턱의 윗면 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point to the top surface of the sill.

phrases.en: I put the plant on the windowsill to get sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 창턱에 두는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb for placing something on the sill.

phrases.en: I wiped the windowsill after the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼지나 물이 쌓이는 창턱을 청소할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for cleaning the sill where dust or water collects.

explain_en: It is the ledge that sticks out horizontally at the bottom of a window. The frame around the window is '창틀' and the area near the window is '창가', so they are different words.

examples.ko: 택배 기사님이 상자를 떨어뜨려서 물건을 파손했어요.
examples.en: The delivery driver dropped the box and damaged the item.
If you damage public facilities, you have to pay a fine.

examples.ko: 태풍이 항구의 배를 여러 척 파손했어요.
examples.en: The typhoon damaged several boats in the harbor.
Move the glass carefully so you don't break it.
I accidentally damaged my friend's phone screen.

examples.ko: 가게 간판을 파손하고 도망간 사람을 경찰이 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are looking for the person who damaged the shop sign and ran away.

explain: '깨다'와 '부수다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '파손하다'는 물건이나 시설이 망가졌다는 사실을 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 택배 상자의 '파손 주의' 스티커도 이 말이에요. 사람이 아니라 물건이 망가졌을 때만 써요.

phrases.en: The cup in the box was damaged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동형으로, 물건이 망가진 결과를 말할 때 써요. '파손하다'는 누가 망가뜨렸는지가 중요할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form: describes something that ended up damaged. '파손하다' focuses on who caused it.

phrases.en: The box says 'Fragile'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택배 상자에 붙이는 말로, 깨지기 쉬우니 조심하라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A label on parcels meaning 'handle with care, fragile'.

phrases.en: Please do not damage the park benches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공공 물건을 망가뜨리지 말라는 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common on public notices telling people not to damage property.

explain_en: 깨다 and 부수다 are everyday words, while 파손하다 states in a formal way that an object or facility got damaged. The 파손 주의 (fragile) sticker on delivery boxes uses it too. It is used only for things being damaged, never for people.
